terms.grammar: neuter of quantus, as a pronoun (with a genitive) or an adverb
evidence: Sen. Ep. 76.5: ‘quantum’ inquis ‘prōficiam?’ quantum temptāveris
Hor. Ep. 1.7.16: at tū, quantum vīs, tolle
terms.comment: With a genitive, how much of: quantum morae, how much delay. Answered by tantum, which takes the genitive the same way (tantum cibī, so much food): quantum … tantum, as much … so much (Cic. Fam. 16.2.1).

terms.gloss: how great? how big? how much …!
evidence: Hor. S. 1.5.43: ō quī complexūs et gaudia quanta fuērunt
Mart. 14.218.1: dīc quotus et quantī cupiās cēnāre
terms.comment: Of price: see “how much is it?”.

phrases.latin: vēscere, sōdēs. — jam satis est. — at tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — benignē.
phrases.english: Do eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Well, take as much as you like. — No, thank you.
“How much shall I gain?” you ask. As much as you try

phrases.latin: nōn quantum vīs sed quantum capis hauriendum est
phrases.english: you should take in not as much as you want but as much as you can hold

phrases.latin: quantum mē dīligis, tantum fac ut valeās
phrases.english: as much as you love me, so much see that you get well

phrases.latin: ō quī complexūs et gaudia quanta fuērunt
phrases.english: oh, what embraces there were, and how much joy!

phrases.latin: incrēdibile est, quantum morae lēctiōnī festīnātiōne adjiciātur
phrases.english: it is unbelievable how much delay hurrying adds to reading

phrases.latin: tantum cibī et pōtiōnis adhibendum ut reficiantur vīrēs, nōn opprimantur
phrases.english: only so much food and drink should be taken as restores one’s strength without crushing it

phrases.latin: tantum nivis fodiendum atque ēgerendum fuit
phrases.english: so much snow had to be dug out and carried away
